findings.F1: In the falling agitated profile, down days are followed by a graded bounce: the slope of the next-day excess return on the day's return over its 30-day swing is -0.0204 (t -2.40, clustered by day, 560 cases), and the mean next-day excess is +1.37 % (t 3.06), about 7 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: The tested side, the up-day giveback, is not graded: on up days in the same profile the slope is +0.0048 (t 0.79, 542 cases). The next day is lower on average (mean excess -0.86 %, t -2.03), but it does not grow with the rise, which is why the tested idea came out inconclusive (t 0.27).
findings.F3: The bounce rises with the size of the fall: by quartile of the scaled fall, the next-day excess is +0.08 %, +1.45 %, +1.41 % and +2.56 % (136 to 142 cases each).
findings.F4: On those down days, the day's high-low range over the 30-day swing grades the bounce more firmly than the close-to-close fall:
findings.F5: The scaled-fall slope leans on one period: in 2020 it is +0.0349 (t 8.09), and in w16 it is t 7.82 with 116 cases. Without 2020 it falls to t 1.49, and without w16 to t 1.78. The other years and windows are positive but small (t -0.72 to 1.41).
findings.F6: The bounce points the same way on every coin: the slope on the scaled fall is positive on all six coins (t 0.98 to 2.77), and the mean next-day excess runs from +0.78 % (BTC) to +2.23 % (LTC).
findings.F7: The bounce lives in the falling agitated profile. Outside it, down days show no bounce:
findings.F8: The bounce is spent after one day: on falling agitated down days, the day-2 slope is +0.0047 (t 0.61) and the day-2 mean excess is -0.25 % (t -0.60).
findings.F9: The short-only book earns little from this profile: Sharpe 0.27 against holding's 0.57, and +1.5 % a year. 88 % of its worst-quintile bars and 96 % of its best-quintile bars fall in the profile, so its swings are this profile's up-day noise, with no graded edge.

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the wider a down day's high-to-low range against the coin's 30-day standard deviation of daily returns, the larger the coin's rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A wide down day in a falling, agitated coin is a reason to buy for one day, and the wider the day, the larger the bounce to expect.
ideas.name: wide down-day range bounce

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a one-day fall against the coin's 30-day standard deviation of daily returns, the larger the coin's rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp down day, pushed by forced sellers, is a reason to take a one-day long rather than follow the fall.
ideas.name: agitated fall scaled bounce
